strings.en:
Once upon a time, there was a teeny-tiny village. The village was ruled by an evil sorcerer named Sumac. Sumac was a cruel and vile leader, and he ruled the little village from the safety of his cabin far in the woods—tucked out of sight. Shhhhh!

One day, a benevolent witch named Lychnis found herself in the village. She knew very well of Sumac's cruelty and thirst, but the villagers were ignorant. Happy, even. They danced in the town square, and the smells of freshly baked pies and bread lingered in the air. But it was only a matter of time before the streets were painted scarlet. She feared for the people of that little village.

Lychnis decided to take measures into her own hands. She reached out to the king of the land, pleading with him to aid her in defeating the cruel sorcerer of the forest. The king denied her call to action and sent the witch on her way.

strings.en:
Ceara, Secondborn,

I hope this letter finds you in poor health and a general state of ruin. It appears that I made a grievous lapse in judgment by letting you and your brigand ilk take shelter in the generous boughs of my arbor. I was promised information, secrets I have been chasing for years, and what do I have to show for it? Nothing but a small army of Lionguard scurrying about my sanctuary where they do not belong. Never mind that you had the nerve—nay, the audacity—to recruit my courtiers away to carry out your pointless schemes.

Do you think you are clever? I know you lured Caithe into a trap. I even know that you ensnared my dearheart within your wretched web for a fleeting moment. It must have been quite the intriguing repartee... Enlightening, to say the least. So, heed these words: I will get the answers I am owed. You have exceeded the limits of my patience. Keep an extra eye on the shadows, my dear. Never rest. Never blink.

Expect me,

Grand Duchess Faolain, Firstborn

Kasmeer Meade,  

I expect that this letter will find you in respectable company and good health. Word has reached the Collective of your family's recent hardships, and we want to assure you that the status of your membership is unchanged. While I am not versed in the intricacies of human scandal, concerns were raised regarding your ability to perform tasks for us while also meeting your financial obligations.   

Your sponsor has since stifled any concerns on your behalf, vouching for your strength of character, skill, and most importantly, discretion. If it would bolster your spirits, know that you have allies in your corner, including one with great influence.  

In the meantime, should any situations arise, we will keep you in mind; your sponsor mentioned you were looking for work around Divinity's Reach. You may contact us if a reference is required. You know the way.  

Regards,  

Fourth Veil, Bengt Tovasson
